(Shutterstock)](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2F8bf979a95bb8bd770f55450f95b92789f72cb4c2-1500x1001.jpg%3Frect%3D0%2C79%2C1500%2C844%26w%3D1920%26h%3D1080%26auto%3Dformat&w=3840&q=75) XRP Ledger has fewer active accounts, but bigger trades and more value. (Shutterstock) Summary * XRP Ledger order-book trading rose 79% from a year earlier in the second quarter, even as the number of accounts initiating trades fell by about 41%, concentrating activity among fewer accounts. * The network’s average tokenized-asset and RLUSD balances reached about $4.26 billion, up from $99 million six quarters earlier, largely because of rapid growth in Ripple’s dollar-backed stablecoin. * Daily active and new accounts declined by about a quarter, but institutional infrastructure expanded through tokenized Treasury settlement, permissioned-market upgrades and U.S. spot XRP exchange-traded funds. The XRP Ledger had fewer active accounts in the second quarter than it did a year earlier, but the accounts still trading on its main exchange were moving almost three times as much XRP. Order-book trading averaged 3.57 million XRP a day during the quarter, up 79% from a year earlier. At the same time, the number of accounts initiating those trades fell to about 1,100 a day from more than 1,860. That worked out to roughly 3,200 XRP traded per account each day, against about 1,070 a year earlier, Evernorth, the XRP treasury company preparing to list on Nasdaq, shared in a quarterly report with CoinDesk.
